PullRequest.Title: sessions: integrate Mission Control host discovery and management
PullRequest.Body:

Mission Control environments now appear in the Agents Window's existing remote-host discovery and management UI. Users can find agent hosts running on other computers, connect to them, and return to their sessions without a separate dashboard or an active connection just to see remembered hosts.

- Restore remembered environments immediately, then refresh discovery without losing the picker's query, selection, or focus. Show refresh failures explicitly while keeping cached hosts available.
- Reuse connect, reconnect, disconnect, and rename controls, with local hide/restore preferences scoped to the current account and profile.
- Retain native session summaries and drafts while disconnected, with read-only access and reconnect guidance. Use the host's advertised agents and session identities, and avoid listing this computer's own host alongside its local connection.
- Identify environments by computer name with the application in parentheses, such as `machine (VS Code Insiders)`. Local aliases remain independent of the advertised name.
- Bound connection and recovery attempts so an unavailable host does not leave the UI waiting indefinitely.

Discovery remains development-only and respects the AI and remote-host feature settings. This reuses the existing Mission Control transport and native session providers; it does not provision compute or change managed-sandbox startup behavior.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The picker call path, handler fan-out, cache bypass, pagination bounds, and repeated back-navigation invocation are explicit. Actual request count varies with pagination, but the minimum cross-provider boundary fan-out and before/after regression are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: HTTP discovery requests and remote-tunnel service calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every initial picker open and every return through showManagePicker starts all registered discovery handlers; cloud-sandbox full discovery alone scans four task scopes with up to 10 sequential pages each, while tunnel and Mission Control discovery add parallel network calls. Reopening/back navigation repeats this boundary fan-out.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network I/O, server load, battery use, and prolonged busy-state activity in a management workflow that previously rendered entirely from cached providers.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this added call, opening or returning to Manage Remote Agent Hosts only built the picker from locally registered providers and performed no discovery boundary work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Showing the picker now calls AgentHostFilterService.rediscover(), which fans out to every registered discovery handler rather than refreshing only stale host inventory or waiting for the explicit Refresh Hosts button.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `void refreshHosts()` after picker.show() runs on every showManagePicker invocation; the same function is called initially and again when returning from host options or menu actions.
Findings.Title: Avoid full discovery every time the management picker opens
Findings.Impact: Simply opening the management UI—or pressing Back after inspecting one host—can issue at least several and up to dozens of unrelated discovery requests, even when cached rows are already available and the user never asks to refresh.
Findings.Evidence: rediscover() executes all handlers with Promise.allSettled. The cloud-sandbox handler calls _discoverAndSeed() with its default incremental=false; CloudSandboxApiService.listSessions then requests four repository/archive scopes and can paginate each to DISCOVERY_TASK_PAGE_LIMIT=10. The tunnel handler calls listTunnels(), and the new Mission Control handler calls listEnvironments({ refresh: true }), explicitly bypassing its 60-second cache. Cloud sandbox coalesces overlap, but completed picker reopenings repeat the scan and the tunnel/Mission Control handlers have no shared in-flight coalescing.
Findings.Recommendation: Render cached providers on show and reserve full rediscovery for the explicit Refresh Hosts button, or invoke stale-aware/coalesced discovery APIs and guard against an existing rediscovery before starting another pass.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The storage event source flag, one-event-per-entry replay semantics, full-scan restore body, and downstream observable publication are all directly established in repository code; only the exact wall-clock magnitude depends on profile key and host counts.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread storage-key scans, JSON parsing, host-array/object allocation, and downstream provider observer/reconciliation work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: If H host metadata values change in one refresh and the profile has P machine-scoped storage keys, storeAll emits H unmerged value-change events and this listener performs H full restores, costing O(H*P) key scans plus O(H^2) host parsing/republication and observer work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased renderer CPU/GC pressure and delayed completion of host refreshes, with potential UI stalls as the retained host inventory grows.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no Mission Control profile-inventory listener or per-host metadata persistence, so a discovery refresh did not feed its own writes back into repeated full inventory restores.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each local metadata write performed by a refresh now synchronously triggers a complete inventory restore; the batched storage API pauses notifications but replays every key event after the batch rather than merging them.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added listener at lines 84-87 calls _restore() for every prefixed profile-storage event, while the same new service persists one metadata entry per host via storeAll(..., false) at lines 269-276.
Findings.Title: Ignore local inventory write notifications
Findings.Impact: On initial discovery or a refresh that changes many host records, the picker remains busy while the renderer repeats the complete restore once per host; retained hosts make this progressively more expensive even though one restore would produce the same state.
Findings.Evidence: AbstractStorageService.storeAll loops over every entry and PauseableEmitter without a merge function replays each queued event. These writes pass external=false, yet this listener does not check e.external. Every callback calls _restore(), which enumerates all PROFILE/MACHINE keys, parses every matching host JSON record, allocates a new host array, and calls hosts.set; that publication also reaches the newly added Mission Control provider reconciliation/description observers.
Findings.Recommendation: Handle only external storage notifications here (as other storage-backed observables do), or suppress/coalesce notifications around _persist. Keep the explicit single _restore() after local preference writes so local rename/hide behavior remains immediate.

Scenarios.Scenario: After-restored Mission Control host initialization and discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench contribution starts refresh fire-and-forget at AfterRestored, so the remote network request is off the core startup critical path, but authentication/account resolution and local-agent IPC must finish before cached profile hosts are restored and providers appear. Refresh completion includes synchronous profile persistence and observable/provider reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read this window's local Mission Control environment ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call during initialize and another after each environment-list request; a normal first refresh therefore performs two.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The former picker queried the local environment ID once for its refresh path and had no persisted inventory initialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initialize call gates cached inventory restoration; the post-list call gates refresh commit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Force-refresh the account's Mission Control environment list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per refresh, independent of the API's 60-second warm cache because refresh:true is always supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior picker also refreshed the environment endpoint when opened, but there was no AfterRestored inventory refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off core startup, but gates discovery completion and provider updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one profile-storage metadata value per retained host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: H writes for H retained hosts; each changed local write emits an event that the new listener turns into a complete inventory restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No profile host inventory was persisted or replayed before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event replay and restore work delay refresh completion and provider publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number H of discovered plus indefinitely retained hosts and P profile machine-scoped storage keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: initialize coalesces only while its promise is in flight. Refreshes are not coalesced; newer generations reject older results after their boundary work. The startup contribution normally launches one pass, while account/configuration events can overlap it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile metadata is a positive warm cache scoped by account/profile and retains absent hosts as unavailable. It is restored only after account and local-host identity resolution. Network refresh always bypasses the API's environment cache; there is no negative-cache state for signed-out/no-host results.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: storage event semantics, full-scan restore, and downstream observable publication are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical host counts may be small, but retained inventories and profile key counts vary; the local event amplification is deterministic whenever multiple metadata values change.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: each local batched persistence pass feeds back into one full restore per changed host.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and navigating the Manage Remote Agent Hosts picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cached provider rows render before discovery resolves, so network work is not required for first paint, but the picker enters a busy state and every show automatically starts discovery. Returning from host options or a menu action constructs and shows the picker again.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full managed-sandbox task discovery across repository/archive scopes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four scopes with 1-10 sequential pages each, so 4-40 HTTP requests per completed picker-show scan; overlapping full scans are coalesced by this handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening or returning to the management picker did not call discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the picker is shown but contributes to its busy period and consumes network/server resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tunnel-list operation per rediscovery invocation; no shared AgentHostFilter coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No tunnel status request was caused by showing this picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with other handlers and gates completion of the picker busy state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP environment-list request per rediscovery, with refresh:true bypassing the 60-second API cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Mission Control request was caused by showing this picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel and gates busy-state completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of picker shows/back navigations and cloud task-list pages across four scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentHostFilter runs all registered handlers concurrently with Promise.allSettled. It permits overlapping rediscover calls; cloud discovery coalesces overlaps, but tunnel and Mission Control handlers do not share an in-flight result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rows come from local providers, but automatic rediscovery bypasses Mission Control's warm cache and cloud manual discovery bypasses stale-refresh throttling. There is no global negative cache or coalesced rediscovery promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added show-time call, handler registration, pagination limit, and cache-bypass flags are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most accounts will use fewer than the 40-page maximum, but even empty inventories require cross-provider requests and every completed re-show repeats them.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary-fanout regression: a formerly local management surface now launches unrelated full discovery on every show.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mission Control host picker refresh and explicit host connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the dedicated picker waits for initialize (account resolution plus local-agent IPC), then shows retained hosts while a background refresh runs. Selecting one visible host performs live environment validation and then relay connection; those operations are on the connect critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the local Mission Control environment ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One during picker initialization, another during refresh, and another in the cloud connection service for a selected connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old picker fetched local identity during its refresh but did not have the separate persisted-inventory initialization stage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first gates picker display; the connect-time call gates relay establishment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh environments and validate the selected environment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list request per picker refresh and one get-environment request for the selected host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old picker also listed environments and validated the selected environment before connecting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: List runs after display; get-environment gates connection and avoids minting credentials for offline hosts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mint connection credentials and establish the relay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected-host connection attempt, with internal authentication validation and relay handshake; bounded by the new 60-second admission deadline and existing connection timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior Mission Control connection command used the same cloud sandbox connection service.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected host per user action; retained host count affects picker row reconstruction but not connection boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The dedicated picker rejects refresh while quickPick.busy. The inventory service permits only one connect per host ID and cancels it on hide/disconnect; connection and recovery deadlines bound long attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Retained profile hosts are warm-cache rows after initialize. Refresh intentionally bypasses the environment cache. Existing relay connections are reused; offline status prevents credential/relay work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and bounds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication and IPC latency vary, but boundary cardinality is fixed per action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: selected-host network work remains cardinality one and bounded; redundant identity checks are not sufficiently costly by themselves.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restoring and retaining disconnected native session summaries
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each visible inventory host, provider construction synchronously reads its account/profile-specific application-storage cache and hydrates bounded session adapters before any relay connection. Disconnect leaves these summaries published and read-only; reconnect is deferred until user/session demand.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and later persist cached session summaries under a per-profile/account/host key
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache hydration per visible host/provider; each host cache is capped by CACHED_SESSIONS_MAX_PER_HOST.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: User-local Mission Control providers were created only from staged/connected entries and did not retain disconnected summaries under account/profile-specific keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hydration is on provider publication but requires no network; persistence is deferred by existing cache bookkeeping.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible host count times the existing per-host cached-session cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider creation and cache hydration occur synchronously during reconciliation; no connections are launched. On-demand connect remains per selected session/host.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive summaries are isolated by profile and account and capped per host. There is no negative cache, but missing storage is a cheap empty result. Hide disposes the provider while metadata remains available for later restore.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and cache bounds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider construction cost depends on cached summaries, but the existing per-host cap prevents unbounded per-key hydration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the eager work is required to expose offline summaries and is bounded per host; the reportable amplification comes from the inventory storage event loop above.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation waits for both parent and selected-target stat results before accepting or rejecting the folder.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the parent directory and selected target
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two concurrent stat calls per validation. When parent access fails, the target stat is newly attempted so a granted child can still be accepted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The parent stat ran first and target stat ran second only if the parent succeeded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both settle before validation completes; concurrent placement removes the prior serial dependency when both are accessible.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One validation action; fixed cardinality of two filesystem operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two operations run concurrently via Promise.allSettled, with no loop or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem/provider latency varies, but cardinality is constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the extra target stat occurs only in the denied-parent case needed for the changed behavior, while the normal path improves latency by parallelizing two fixed operations.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 36 changed files. Reported synchronous repeated inventory restoration caused by local storage events and automatic cross-provider network discovery on every management-picker show. Checked startup, dedicated picker/connect, retained session caches, UI-derived descriptions, recovery deadlines, and file-dialog filesystem work; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
